title: The Letters Themselves
label: ch:abecedario
canDo: I can name every letter of the Spanish alphabet, spell a name aloud over a telephone, tell b from v when somebody asks, and say where a word may and may not be broken.

payoff.summary: Spell a surname aloud letter by letter, say that a vowel carries its accent, and settle the b-or-v question the way a Spanish speaker does.
payoff.note: Closes A1-O1-01 (the alphabet and the names of the letters), A1-O1-02 (the vowel letters), A1-O1-03 (consonants and digraphs) and A1-O1-07 (syllable division and double spellings), taking the Ortografia de letras y palabras category from 0/7 to 4/7. The letter NAMES are the load-bearing part rather than the shapes: a listening paper dictates a name letter by letter, and hache, jota and equis are not guessable from English. The b-and-v lesson exists because the two are homophones in Spanish, which is why the language grew be larga and ve corta -- a disambiguation an English speaker never needs and a Spanish speaker uses constantly.
